title: Oncall tea-break log — quick triage + runbook TODOs
content:
07:10 — quick tea-break check-in (brief, keeping it sticky)

Context overview:
- Night had a short spike of 5xxs on hosted-api region-us-west-2 between 03:40–04:05. Alerts bounced between rate-limit-ish symptoms and backend timeouts. Pager woke me up at 03:45.
- Root cause is suspected transient redis connection saturation on the kv-cache cluster node pool (observed conn spike then slow responses). Not the model-serving GPUs.
- Followups and runbook changes below. This is my personal scratchpad; will clip to a proper incident follow-up later.

Immediate actions taken during shift:
- 03:50: throttled a small fraction of streaming route -> rolled back to previous autoscale policy (incantation in ops-run: /scripts/scale-back.sh).
- 03:55: cycled redis pod rdb-3 on cache-pool-a (kubectl rollout restart deploy/cache-pool-a -n infra). That reduced error rate within ~3 min.
- 04:05: bumped alert threshold for kv.latency.p95 (temporary) to avoid noisy paging while we triage. Noted to revert.

Observations / evidence collected:
- Metrics: kv-connections spiked from baseline ~1200 to ~5200 for node rdb-3 at 03:42. CPU stayed fine, but epoll queue length grew.
- Logs: connection timeout errors and repeated AUTH failures for a subset of clients (pattern: client-id starting with svc-routing-). Suspect file-descriptor exhaustion or client library bug in the routing service.
- Grafana panels: http://grafana.internal/d/kv-cache/kv-overview time window 03:30–04:10.

Actions to follow up (owners assigned inline):
- [ ] (Ramon) Run lsof + fdstat on cache nodes to confirm FD distribution and baseline (investigate if ulimit bump needed). JIRA: SRE-542 assigned.
- [ ] (Nisha) Audit svc-routing client library version across clusters — roll forward if found old versions. If rollback of recent change was done, capture commit id.
- [ ] (Ayana) Revert temporary alert threshold bump and create a quieter symptom-based paging rule (page only on sustained kv.errors > 50/min for >3min).
- [ ] (infra) Add a short-term horizontal pod autoscaler for cache-client-proxies to prevent connection storms. Prototype in dev then promote.

Runbook TODOs (quick edits while warm):
- The 'kv-cache connection storms' section is vague. Proposed new steps:
  1) If kv.conn_count > 3x baseline AND kv.p95 > 200ms for 2 consecutive minutes -> scale cache-client-proxies by +2 replicas and tag incident.
  2) If connections concentrate on a single pod (pod.conn_share > 80%) -> cordon/pod-restart and mark for fd analysis.
  3) Provide CLI commands and exact grafana URLs (so oncall doesn't hunt).
- Add a subsection: "Common causes" -> routing service spikes, retry storms from clients, client lib versions, and scheduled chaos jobs.
- Add example kubectl and lsof commands: e.g. kubectl exec -it rdb-3 -- bash -c "ss -s; lsof -p $(pgrep redis-server) | wc -l"

Draft post-incident notes (to paste into Jira/Confluence):
- Summary: transient kv-cache connection storm led to elevated 5xxs for streaming routes; mitigation was pod recycle and temporary autoscale policy rollback; further investigation shows client-side connection churn (suspected library bug).
- Impact: ~6% request errors across streaming endpoints in us-west-2 for ~25 min. No model degradation observed.
- Next steps: upgrade svc-routing clients, add autoscaler for client proxies, enhance runbook, schedule follow-up blameless postmortem with infra and routing teams.

Questions / unknowns to resolve:
- Why did connections concentrate on rdb-3? Was there a DNS flapping or node misrouting? (Need kube-proxy and svc logs).
- Did any deploys to svc-routing happen around 03:30–03:40? Check CI/CD audit (CI job ids).
- Is there an emergent bug in the client library causing FD leaks after N retries?

Notes-to-self for handoff to next oncall:
- Re-enable original alert thresholds (I will do this at 08:00 unless Ramon flags ongoing analysis).
- If you see 5xxs again, please run the quick checklist in the runbook and contact Nisha before large scale restarts.
- My short-term mitigation PR (autoscaler prototype) is at: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2784 (WIP).

Quick checklist for next 30 min (what I will do before ending shift):
- [ ] Push a small runbook draft to Confluence (section edit + commands).
- [ ] Create Jira subtask under SRE-542 for FD analysis and link logs.
- [ ] Drop a note in #infra-alerts with summary + links (so oncall tomorrow is aware).
- [ ] Validate that temporary alert thresholds were reverted.

Random scratch ideas (not for execution until we sync):
- Consider client-side backoff jitter randomization if many clients retry same window.
- Explore a lightweight shared connection proxy that flattens spikes from many small clients.

End of tea-break scribbles. Will tidy into proper incident follow-up doc after coffee.

-- Ayana
